standardHeading: Not a soft skills workshop. A floor protocol.
standardIntro: Every rule in this framework exists because a nervous system does something predictable when it is startled, crowded or asked to perform. You are not learning to be nicer. You are learning to stop producing the signal that makes a guest shut down in your space.

pillars.title: No performance required
pillars.body: Guests are released from the fake it till you make it conversation while their brain is busy processing everything else in the room. Silence is a listed service, not an awkward gap.

pillars.title: Nothing happens without warning
pillars.body: Every chair movement, every tool, every hand. Announced before it happens, with scripts provided for you. Predictable service structure to ensure surprise never becomes startle.

pillars.title: Recovery without apology
pillars.body: A sensory spike is a neutral event with a written protocol attached, not an incident anyone has to feel bad about afterwards. Nobody manages it by improvising.

captureBody: Sit in your own service chair for ten minutes during a busy hour and answer twelve questions. You will get the PDF straight away, plus the client-facing Sensory Safety Expectations sheet you can post on your booking page.

founderQuote: Your calm is the most expensive service you provide.
founderBody:
I grew up in chaos, and for a long time the only language I knew was hustle, because hustle was what kept me alive. I built Retro Redhead so no other stylist would have to choose between feeding their kid and replacing their own worn-out shoes.

This is not a soft skills guide. It is an operations manual, grounded in biology, written in plain language and tested on a real floor with real guests.
